title: In any book, the second word bows to the first
body: Zipf's law observes that a word's frequency is roughly inversely proportional to its rank: 'the' doubles the runner-up, triples the third, in text after text and language after language. Similar rank laws show up in city sizes and web hits. No one fully agrees why; preferential growth keeps being found at the scene.
source_hint: Zipf, 'Human Behavior and the Principle of Least Effort' (1949)
